_note:
The country under the country. **Three ways in and one town, and the town is empty** — a shop with no shelves, no errands, and prose that says the writing stops here. `PLAN-M14.md` §1.5: it is not a placeholder drawn as a town, it is a town drawn honestly, and what goes in it is the next plan's. Twenty tiles of it are road between the three gates and the town and **nothing else on it is load-bearing**, which is §9 decision 2 left where it was found: a country drawn to a guess is a country somebody has to unpick.

**A table since M17, and the second one.** `traversal: "shot"` — the country under the country is crossed by pulling back and firing, the same as the Treyway above it. `PLAN-M17.md` §4.2 asks for three things and it gets all three: **sand past each of the three ways up**, so an arrival at one is a stopped ball rather than a lucky one; **the central road is the one fast lane**, at cost 1 against the scrub's 1 and the slag's 2, running the whole height of the map through the town's own door; and six obstacles, with **a bumper on each of the two far slag ranges** and the pocket in the south-west, which is the corner of this map with nothing on it and is therefore the corner it would be a shame to end up in.

**The drifts are past the gates and not before them.** Sand stops a ball dead, so a drift on the approach is a wall in front of a door; one on the far side is a backstop. Both ways up are on the southern road with open scrub below them, and Marbulon's door is at the top with open scrub above — which is the only reason all three could take the same treatment.

**And nothing about the country moved.** Nine tiles gained a place; not one of them changed terrain, and the town, the three gates and the door at the end of the writing are where M14 put them. A map becoming a table is a line in its header, which is the whole point of `Traversal` being on the file rather than in the save.

places.name: a town with no name on the post yet
the way back up the Sump
the way back up the Stair
the underside of a door in the shallows
the way on
prose: The road runs south out of the town for four miles and then stops, and what it stops at is not a wall and not a coast and not an edge.
This is where the writing stops. Not the game — the writing. What is past this is not hidden and not locked and not saved for later: nobody has decided it yet.

You dropped a tower, drained a lake, took two dungeons apart from the inside and came up under a door an old woman has been sitting in front of for eleven years. The last fact this game has for you is that she was right about the number.

places.name: the low boulder
places.shut: A boulder the size of a cart, and the ground round it is scoured smooth. Everything that comes down here has been off it.

places.name: the high boulder
places.shut: Its twin, or near enough. Nobody carried either of them here.

places.name: the drift under the sump
places.shut: Grit, a foot of it, banked against the wall. Whatever rolls in stops.

places.name: the drift under the stair
places.shut: The same grit, the same wall, the other end of it.

places.name: the drift under the door
places.shut: It has been coming down through the shallows for years, and this is where it has got to.

places.name: the lost corner
places.shut: A hole in the slag with nothing at the bottom you can see. Things go in here and the country does not give them back.
